'''Francis S. Gabreski Airport''' {{airport codes|FOK|KFOK|FOK}} is a county-owned, joint civil-military [[airport]] located {{convert|3|NM|km|0|lk=on}} north of the [[central business district]] of [[Westhampton Beach, New York|Westhampton Beach]], in [[Suffolk County, New York|Suffolk County]], [[New York (state)|New York]], [[United States]].<ref name=FAA /> It is approximately {{convert|80|mi|km}} east of [[New York City]], on [[Long Island]].

Known as [[Suffolk County Air Force Base]] until 1969, then '''Suffolk County Airport''' until 1991, when it was renamed in honor of [[Colonel]] [[Francis S. Gabreski]], [[USAF]] (Retired), a [[U.S. Army Air Forces]] [[flying ace]] in [[World War II]] who, as a [[U.S. Air Force]] officer, was later the commander of the [[52nd Fighter-Interceptor Wing]] at [[Suffolk County Air Force Base]] from 1964 through November 1967, when he retired.<ref>{{cite news |last=Freedman |first=Mitchell |date=February 23, 1992 |title=WWII Ace Lands an Honor |work=Newsday |id={{ProQuest|278444133}}}}</ref>

The airport is both a [[general aviation]] facility utilized by corporate businesses, [[private aviation]] and [[air taxi]] services, and an [[Air National Guard]] (ANG) base for the [[106th Rescue Wing]] (106 RQW), an [[Air Combat Command]] (ACC)-gained unit of the [[New York Air National Guard]].

== History ==
{{Main|Francis S. Gabreski Air National Guard Base}}

===Suffolk County Army Air Field===
The [[New York World War II Army Airfields|Suffolk County Army Air Field]] was built in 1943 as a [[United States Army Air Forces]] sub-base of nearby [[Mitchel AFB|Mitchel Field]].  Later assigned to [[First Air Force]], the 437th Army Air Force Base Unit defended the [[New York City]] area and flew antisubmarine patrols. [[Post-war]], the airfield was conveyed to [[Suffolk County, New York|Suffolk County]] for use as a civilian airport, but included a reversal clause if future military use was ever needed.

===Suffolk County Air Force Base===
Renamed when the [[United States Air Force]] reclaimed the airport in 1951, [[Suffolk County Air Force Base]] was part of the [[Eastern Air Defense Force]]'s defense of the [[New York City metropolitan area]].  The [[Air National Guard]]'s [[103d Fighter Wing|103rd Fighter-Interceptor Wing]] (103 FIW), along with the 118th Fighter-Interceptor Squadron and its [[P-47|F-47N Thunderbolts]],<ref>{{Dead link |date=May 2013}}{{cite web |url=http://www.cradleofaviation.org/history/airfields/adc.html |title=Suffolk County Air Force Base (ADC) - the Cradle of Aviation Museum |access-date=2005-10-18 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20051223184542/http://www.cradleofaviation.org/history/airfields/adc.html |archive-date=2005-12-23 }} Suffolk County Air Force Base (ADC)</ref> was federalized on March 2, 1951, and moved from [[Brainard Field]], Connecticut, to Suffolk County AFB on June 1.  The 103 FIW was returned to state control on February 6, 1952, and remained briefly at Suffolk County until replaced by the 45th and 75th Fighter-Interceptor Squadrons in November 1952, flying the [[F-86 Sabre]] as part of the [[23d Wing|23rd Fighter-Interceptor Group]] (23 FIG).

In 1955, the 23 FIG was reassigned to [[Presque Isle Air Force Base]], [[Maine]] and replaced by the newly activated [[52nd Fighter Wing|52nd Fighter-Interceptor Wing]] (52 FIW), which flew under various designations from Suffolk County AFB until 1969, with the 2d and 5th Fighter-Interceptor Squadrons flying [[F-94 Starfire]], [[F-101 Voodoo]] and [[F-102 Delta Dagger]] interceptors. In 1963, the 52 FIW was renamed the 52nd Fighter Wing (Air Defense) and became part of the [[New York Air Defense Sector]] (NY ADS), the NY ADS being one of four USAF air defense sectors employing the [[Semi-Automatic Ground Environment]] (SAGE) system.

Suffolk County AFB was also the main support base for the [[Suffolk County Missile Annex]], a nearby USAF [[CIM-10 Bomarc]] surface-to-air missile [[launch complex]] for the defense of the New York City metropolitan area under the control of a [[missile launch control center]] at [[McGuire Air Force Base]], New Jersey.

As a result of funding shortfalls for the [[Vietnam War]] that resulted in the closure of numerous stateside air force bases and naval air stations, Suffolk County AFB deactivated in 1969 and the [[military installation]] was again transferred to the Suffolk County government for use as a civilian airport.

===Suffolk County Airport/Air National Guard Base and Francis S. Gabreski Airport/Air National Guard Base===
'''[[Aviation in the New York metropolitan area|Suffolk County Airport]]''' (Francis S. Gabreski Airport after 1991) operated as a civilian general aviation airport without a military unit from 1969 until 1970.

Military operations were reintroduced in June 1970 when the [[102nd Air Refueling Squadron]] (102 AREFS) of the [[106th Air Refueling Group]] (106 ARG), [[New York Air National Guard]], relocated to Suffolk County with their [[KC-97 Stratofreighter]]s after the closing of [[Naval Air Station]] [[Floyd Bennett Field]]. In 1972, the unit's mission changed from air refueling to fighter-interceptor, with the new mission of controlling the skies along the northeast U.S. coast with [[F-102 Delta Dagger]] aircraft.

In 1975, the designation and mission changed again to "Aerospace Rescue and Recovery", later shortened to "Air Rescue" and then simply "Rescue". The current names of the [[102nd Rescue Squadron]] (102 RQS) and [[106th Rescue Wing]] (106 RQW) were assigned in 1995. Today, the 106 RQW provides peacetime and combat [[search and rescue]] services using [[HC-130J]] Hercules aircraft and [[Sikorsky HH-60 Pave Hawk|HH-60W Pave Hawk]] helicopters. The rescue wing was featured in the book and movie of ''[[The Perfect Storm (book)|The Perfect Storm]]'' which details the crash of one of the wing's HH-60G Pave Hawk rescue helicopters while conducting search and rescue operations from the airport during the [[1991 Perfect Storm]].

[[Air Force One]] was also often located at the Air National Guard base in the summers of 1998 and 1999 during weeklong visits by President [[Bill Clinton]] and First Lady [[Hillary Clinton]] during extended stays at the [[Georgica Pond]] home of film director [[Steven Spielberg]] in [[East Hampton (village), New York|East Hampton, New York]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Ketcham |first=Diane |date=1998-08-09 |title=LONG ISLAND JOURNAL; An East-Ender Who's a Real Friend of Bill |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1998/08/09/nyregion/long-island-journal-an-east-ender-who-s-a-real-friend-of-bill.html |access-date=2024-06-25 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref>

== Facilities and aircraft ==
[[File:102d Rescue Squadron - HC-130 Snowstorm.jpg|thumb|An [[Lockheed HC-130|HC-130]] at the airport in 2010.]]
[[File:NetJets Citation Latitude N665QS Westhampton Beach (Quintin Soloviev).jpg|thumb|One of [[NetJets]] many [[Citation Latitude]]'s ready to board at the airport]]
Although given a Westhampton Beach ZIP Code (11978), the airport is located just outside Westhampton Beach Village limits, in an unincorporated area in the [[Southampton (town), New York|Town of Southampton]].

Gabreski Airport covers an area of {{convert|1,451|acre|ha}} which contains three paved [[runway]]s. Runway 6/24 measures 9,002 x 150 ft (2,744 x 46 m), making it among [[New York City|New York]]'s longest after [[JFK International Airport]] and [[Stewart International Airport]]. The airport has two additional runways (1/19 and 15/33), 1/19 measuring 5,100 x 150 ft (1,524 x 46 m) and 15/33 measuring 5,002 x 150 ft (1,525 x 46).<ref name=FAA />

For the 12-month period ending December 31, 2023, the airport had 50,156 aircraft operations, an average of 137 per day: 69% [[general aviation]], 19% [[air taxi]], and 12% [[military aviation|military]]. At that time there were 85 aircraft based at this airport: 57 single-[[aircraft engine|engine]], 2 multi-engine, 7 [[jet aircraft|jet]], 8 [[helicopter]], and 11 [[military aircraft|military]].<ref name=FAA />

As of September 2022, one [[fixed-base operator]] provides services to airport users: Modern Aviation.<ref>[http://www.sheltairaviation.com Shelt-Air Aviation Services]</ref> It is the only FBO operation at the airport, with its predecessor, [[SheltAir|Sheltair]], having bought Malloy Air East in early 2014.

The [[Suffolk County Police Department|Suffolk County Police]] Aviation Section bases a Law Enforcement and [[MEDEVAC]] [[Police helicopter|helicopter]] at the airport.  The base is staffed from 7AM to 11PM by two police officer pilots as well as a flight [[Paramedics in the United States|paramedic]] employed by [[Stony Brook University Hospital]]. The airport is patrolled by the [[Suffolk County, New York Sheriff's Office|Suffolk County Sheriff's Office]].

== Accidents and incidents ==

* On August 11, 2010, [[Air Force Two]], which was departing Gabreski Airport for [[Washington, D.C.]] with then-Vice President [[Joseph R. Biden, Jr.]] on board, caused damage to an unoccupied [[Piper J-3 Cub|Piper Cub]] at the airport while taxiing, due to the large plane's [[jet blast]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |date=August 12, 2010 |title=Biden in Wing Bender |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB10001424052748704901104575423852013816256 |access-date=2024-06-24 |work=[[The Wall Street Journal]]}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Russell |first=Jennett Meriden |date=2010-08-17 |title=Air Force Two damages aircraft at Gabreski Airport |url=https://www.27east.com/southampton-press/southampton-police/air-force-two-damages-aircraft-at-gabreski-airport-1585427/ |access-date=2024-06-25 |website=27 East |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=abc7NY |title=Air Force Two in minor incident on Long Island with Vice President Joe Biden aboard |url=https://abc7ny.com/archive/7605336/ |access-date=2024-06-25 |website=ABC7 New York |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite web |date=2010-08-11 |title=Joe Biden's Air Force Two Plane in Incident at L.I. Airport |url=https://www.nbcnewyork.com/news/local/joe-bidens-air-force-2-plane-involved-in-incident-at-li-airport/1944678/ |access-date=2024-06-25 |website=NBC New York |agency=Associated Press |language=en-US}}</ref> There were no injuries, but the left wing of the Piper received damage.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" /><ref name=":3" />
* On February 26, 2017, a plane bound for the airport crashed into the nearby woods, subsequently catching fire.<ref name=":4">{{Cite news |last=Dollinger |first=Arielle |last2=Foderaro |first2=Lisa W. |date=2017-02-27 |title=Small Plane Crashes on Long Island, Killing Two |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2017/02/26/nyregion/small-plane-crashes-on-long-island-killing-two.html |access-date=2024-06-25 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref><ref name=":5">{{Cite news |last=Rojas |first=Rick |last2=Dollinger |first2=Arielle |date=2017-03-03 |title=With a Trail of Smoke, a Leisurely Flight Turned Deadly |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2017/03/03/nyregion/with-a-trail-of-smoke-a-leisurely-flight-turned-deadly.html |access-date=2024-06-25 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref><ref name=":6">{{Cite web |last=Thorne |first=Kristin |date=2017-02-27 |title=NTSB investigating deadly plane crash in Suffolk County |url=https://abc7ny.com/westhampton-plane-crash-gabreski-airport-in-westhampton-suffolk-county/1775194/ |access-date=2024-06-25 |website=ABC7 New York |language=en}}</ref> The pilot was critically injured and the two passengers were killed.<ref name=":4" /><ref name=":5" /><ref name=":6" />
* On October 13, 2018, a [[Piper PA-28 Cherokee|Piper PA-28]] bound for [[Charleston, South Carolina]] from [[Danbury Municipal Airport]] in [[Danbury, Connecticut]] crashed into the [[Atlantic Ocean]] approximately {{Convert|3|mi|km}} south-southeast of Gabreski Airport.<ref name=":7">{{Cite web |last=Majchrowicz |first=Michael |date=2018-10-14 |title=3 dead after plane headed for Charleston crashes in Atlantic Ocean |url=https://www.postandcourier.com/news/3-dead-after-plane-headed-for-charleston-crashes-in-atlantic-ocean/article_ee9298c6-cfbf-11e8-b8d8-fb0570f8c513.html |access-date=2024-06-25 |website=Post and Courier |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":8">{{Cite web |date=2018-10-13 |title=2 More Bodies Recovered from Plane Crash that Killed Waterbury Man: Police |url=https://www.nbcconnecticut.com/news/local/1-dead-after-small-plane-crashes-in-waters-off-hamptons-officials/164714/ |access-date=2024-06-25 |website=NBC Connecticut |language=en-US}}</ref> All three people on board were killed.<ref name=":7" /><ref name=":8" />
